title: Scaling Multi-Task Robot RL on GPUs

beats.text: Why do 50% of your GPU cycles waste compute before Scaling Multi-Task Robot RL on GPUs fixes the bottleneck?
beats.visual_focus: A robotic arm twitching violently between four different object manipulation states.

beats.text: It is a relay race where high-performing tasks are dragged down by the clumsy progress of lagging ones.
beats.visual_focus: A graph showing one task success line spiking while three others plummet.

beats.text: Enter DGPO: Demonstration-Guided Policy Optimization. It uses sparse demonstrations to anchor learning, then dynamically releases the training wheels.
beats.visual_focus: A neural network architecture diagram showing demonstration data feeding into value learning.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I hate it when robots glitch out, so that kept me watching. I like that you didn't use 'smart drawers' or any of that cringe AI-influencer talk. However, you lost me at 'IW-ABC'. You dropped a specific acronym and 'progress signal' without explaining if that's a loss function, a reward modifier, or something else. I'm a dev, I don't need it dumbed down, but I need to know the mechanism, not just the name of the paper's specific module.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A relay race where the fastest runner is forced to drag the slowest teammate by the ankle.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Unified multi-task policies that actually transfer to physical hardware.
